                                                                                                   60
                Amend printed bill, strike everything below the enacting clause and substitute:    61
                                                                                                   62
                        "SECTION 1. Legislative declaration. (1) The general assembly              63
                finds and declares that:                                                           64
                        (a) Compounding pharmacies play an important role in the United            65
                States drug supply chain and allow patients to receive life-saving or              66
                life-improving medication when the commercial market is unable to support          67
Senate Journal-52nd Day-March 6, 2026                                                  Page 339


    patients' needs;                                                                               1
            (b) The United States food and drug administration, referred to in this                2
    section as the "FDA", provides regulatory oversight and sets internationally                   3
    recognized standards for drug approval; however, there has been an increase in                 4
    the number of companies that develop, dispense, and market                                     5
    non-FDA-approved compounded medications, notably weight-loss drugs;                            6
            (c) Patients in Colorado are at risk of receiving compounded                           7
    weight-loss medications that are not approved by the FDA or are not                            8
    manufactured in compliance with the FDA's current good manufacturing                           9
    practice requirements;                                                                        10
            (d) The safety and integrity of compounded weight-loss medications                    11
    and their ingredients are paramount for the health and well-being of patients in              12
    Colorado;                                                                                     13
            (e) Patients in Colorado deserve to have clear information regarding the              14
    safety of compounded weight-loss medications and their ingredients;                           15
            (f) Preserving the physician-patient relationship is critical to health               16
    outcomes and protecting a prescriber's scope of care with individual patients                 17
    helps to ensure the health of Coloradans; and                                                 18
            (g) Therefore, the general assembly should take action to protect                     19
    Coloradans by requiring that compounded weight-loss medications are sourced                   20
    from FDA-registered and -inspected facilities and that those medications                      21
    contain safe and pharmaceutical-grade ingredients.                                            22
            SECTION 2. In Colorado Revised Statutes, add 6-1-741 as follows:                      23
            6-1-741. Regulation of compounded weight-loss medication -                            24
    prohibited conduct - labeling requirements - deceptive advertising -                          25
    enforcement by attorney general - rules - definitions.                                        26
            (1) Definitions. AS USED IN THIS SECTION, UNLESS THE CONTEXT                          27
    OTHERWISE REQUIRES:                                                                           28
            (a) (I) "BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE" OR "ACTIVE PHARMACEUTICAL                               29
    INGREDIENT" MEANS A SUBSTANCE THAT IS INTENDED FOR INCORPORATION INTO                         30
    A FINISHED DRUG PRODUCT AND IS INTENDED TO PROMOTE PHARMACOLOGICAL                            31
    ACTIVITY OR OTHER DIRECT EFFECTS IN THE DIAGNOSIS, CURE, MITIGATION,                          32
    TREATMENT, OR PREVENTION OF DISEASE OR TO AFFECT THE STRUCTURE OR                             33
    FUNCTION OF THE BODY.                                                                         34
            (II) "BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE" DOES NOT INCLUDE INTERMEDIATES USED                        35
    IN THE SYNTHESIS OF THE SUBSTANCE.                                                            36
            (b) "COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION" MEANS A DRUG THAT:                            37
            (I) IS CREATED BY COMBINING, MIXING, OR ALTERING OTHER DRUGS OR                       38
    BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES;                                                                         39
            (II) IS INTENDED TO BE USED BY HUMANS FOR OBESITY OR WEIGHT                           40
    MANAGEMENT OR CONTAINS, OR CLAIMS TO CONTAIN, AN ACTIVE INGREDIENT                            41
    THAT IS NAMED IN A DRUG APPROVED BY THE FDA FOR OBESITY OR WEIGHT                             42
    MANAGEMENT; AND                                                                               43
            (III) IS A GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONIST DRUG, ALSO                        44
    KNOWN AS A "GLP-1 DRUG".                                                                      45
            (c) "DRUG" HAS THE MEANING SET FORTH IN SECTION 12-280-103 (16).                      46
            (d) "FDA" MEANS THE FEDERAL FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION.                             47
           (2) Prohibited conduct.                                                                48
           (a) A PERSON SHALL NOT ENGAGE IN THE SALE, TRANSFER, OR                                49
    DISTRIBUTION OF A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION COMPOUNDED                                50
    UNDER SECTION 503A OF THE "FEDERAL FOOD, DRUG, AND COSMETIC ACT", 21                          51
    U.S.C. SEC. 353a, UNLESS THE PERSON COMPOUNDING THE WEIGHT-LOSS                               52
    MEDICATION:                                                                                   53
           (I) USES BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES THAT:                                                    54
           (A) COMPLY WITH THE STANDARDS OF AN APPLICABLE UNITED STATES                           55
    PHARMACOPEIA OR NATIONAL FORMULARY MONOGRAPH, IF A MONOGRAPH                                  56
    EXISTS, AND THE UNITED STATES PHARMACOPEIA CHAPTER ON PHARMACY                                57
    COMPOUNDING;                                                                                  58
           (B) IF A NATIONAL FORMULARY MONOGRAPH DOES NOT EXIST, ARE                              59
    COMPONENTS OF DRUGS APPROVED BY THE FDA; OR                                                   60
           (C) IF A NATIONAL FORMULARY MONOGRAPH DOES NOT EXIST AND THE                           61
    BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES ARE NOT COMPONENTS OF DRUGS APPROVED BY THE                              62
    FDA, APPEAR ON THE LIST DEVELOPED BY THE SECRETARY OF THE FEDERAL                             63
    DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES PURSUANT TO 21 U.S.C. SEC.                            64
    353a (b)(1)(A)(i)(III);                                                                       65
           (II) CONFIRMS THAT, IF A BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE IS USED IN                                66
    ACCORDANCE WITH SUBSECTION (2)(a)(I)(B) OF THIS SECTION, THE BULK DRUG                        67
Page 340   Senate Journal-52nd Day-March 6, 2026


               SUBSTANCE WAS REVIEWED AS PART OF A NEW DRUG APPLICATION THAT THE          1
               FDA HAS APPROVED PURSUANT TO SECTION 505 OF THE "FEDERAL FOOD,             2
               DRUG, AND COSMETIC ACT", 21 U.S.C. SEC. 355;                               3
                       (III) VERIFIES THAT THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES IN THE COMPOUNDED     4
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION ARE HUMAN PHARMACEUTICAL-GRADE PRODUCTS;            5
                       (IV) VERIFIES THAT THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES IN THE COMPOUNDED      6
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION HAVE A VALID CERTIFICATE OF ANALYSIS,               7
               INCLUDING THE IDENTIFICATION AND PURITY OF THOSE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES      8
               AND THE IDENTIFICATION OF EACH IMPURITY BY CHEMICAL NAME AND AMOUNT        9
               PRESENT;                                                                  10
                       (V) VERIFIES THAT THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES IN THE COMPOUNDED      11
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION WERE MANUFACTURED BY A MANUFACTURER THAT           12
               IS REGISTERED WITH THE FDA IN ACCORDANCE WITH 21 U.S.C. SEC. 360; AND     13
                       (VI) VERIFIES THAT THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES IN THE COMPOUNDED     14
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION WERE MANUFACTURED BY A MANUFACTURER THAT           15
               HAS BEEN INSPECTED BY THE FDA AS A HUMAN DRUG ESTABLISHMENT AND THE       16
               INSPECTION CONFIRMED THAT THE MANUFACTURER WAS:                           17
                       (A) IN COMPLIANCE WITH CURRENT GOOD MANUFACTURING PRACTICE        18
               REQUIREMENTS THAT COVERED THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES; AND                   19
                       (B) CLASSIFIED AS "VOLUNTARY ACTION INDICATED" OR "NO ACTION      20
               INDICATED" BY THE FDA.                                                    21
                       (b) BEFORE A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION CONTAINING A       22
               BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE IS OFFERED FOR SALE IN THE STATE, THE                 23
               MANUFACTURER OR WHOLESALER OF THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS                  24
               MEDICATION SHALL CONDUCT AND DOCUMENT QUALITY CONTROL TESTING OF          25
               THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE PRIOR TO USING THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE IN THE     26
               COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION, WHICH TESTING MUST CONFIRM:            27
                       (I) THE IDENTITY AND CONTENT OF THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE; AND      28
                       (II) THAT ANY IMPURITIES PRESENT IN THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCE ARE   29
               IDENTIFIED, CHARACTERIZED, QUANTIFIED, AND JUSTIFIED GIVEN THE PRODUCT    30
               AND ITS INTENDED USE.                                                     31
                       (c) A PERSON THAT COMPOUNDS, SELLS, DISTRIBUTES, OR TRANSFERS     32
               A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION SHALL NOT:                            33
                       (I) DISTRIBUTE A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION TO A           34
               PERSON WHEN THE DISTRIBUTOR IS NOT LEGALLY AUTHORIZED TO DISTRIBUTE       35
               OR TRANSFER THE BULK DRUG SUBSTANCES USED IN THE COMPOUNDED               36
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION;                                                   37
                       (II)   DISTRIBUTE, DISPENSE, OR ADMINISTER A COMPOUNDED           38
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION THAT IS COUNTERFEIT, ADULTERATED, MISBRANDED,      39
               DIVERTED, OR OTHERWISE IN VIOLATION OF FEDERAL OR STATE LAW;              40
                       (III) FAIL TO MAINTAIN REASONABLE SAFEGUARDS TO PREVENT           41
               CONTAMINATION, DIVERSION, THEFT, OR MISUSE OF THE COMPOUNDED              42
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION IN VIOLATION OF APPLICABLE FEDERAL OR STATE        43
               LAW;                                                                      44
                       (IV) SHIP OR DISTRIBUTE FINISHED COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS           45
               MEDICATION OR ACTIVE PHARMACEUTICAL INGREDIENTS TO A PERSON NOT           46
               LEGALLY AUTHORIZED UNDER FEDERAL OR STATE LAW TO RECEIVE, COMPOUND,       47
               MANUFACTURE, DISTRIBUTE, OR DISPENSE SUCH DRUGS;                          48
                       (V) MAKE A MATERIALLY FALSE OR MISLEADING REPRESENTATION          49
               THAT THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION IS APPROVED BY THE FDA         50
               WHEN THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION IS NOT APPROVED BY THE         51
               FDA;                                                                      52
                     (VI) MAKE A MATERIALLY FALSE, MISLEADING, OR UNVERIFIED CLAIM       53
               REGARDING THE EFFICACY, SAFETY, COMPARATIVE PERFORMANCE, CLINICAL         54
               OUTCOMES, OR OTHER THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF THE COMPOUNDED                 55
               WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION; OR                                                56
                     (VII)     REPRESENT DIRECTLY OR BY IMPLICATION THAT THE             57
               COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION HAS SUPERIOR EFFICACY OR SAFETY         58
               COMPARED TO ANOTHER MEDICALLY APPROPRIATE PRODUCT, UNLESS THAT            59
               SUPERIORITY HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED BY WELL-CONTROLLED CLINICAL             60
               STUDIES AND IS SUPPORTED BY COMPETENT SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE.                61
                     (3) Labeling requirements.                                          62
                     (a) THE LABEL OF A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION MUST:          63
                     (I) LIST EACH OF THE ACTIVE INGREDIENTS IN THE MEDICATION AND THE   64
               FOLLOWING INFORMATION ABOUT EACH INGREDIENT:                              65
                     (A) THE ESTABLISHED NAME OF THE INGREDIENT; AND                     66
                     (B) THE QUANTITY OR PROPORTION OF THE INGREDIENT; AND               67
Senate Journal-52nd Day-March 6, 2026                                         Page 341


           (II) CONTAIN THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS, PRINTED IN A CLEAR AND                  1
    CONSPICUOUS MANNER ON THE LABEL:                                                      2
           (A) "THIS IS A COMPOUNDED DRUG. COMPOUNDED DRUGS ARE NOT                       3
    APPROVED BY THE UNITED STATES FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION AND                        4
    HAVE NO EVIDENCE OF SAFETY OR EFFICACY."                                              5
           (B) "THIS ITEM IS NOT FOR RESALE."                                             6
           (b) A PERSON THAT SELLS, TRANSFERS, OR DISTRIBUTES A COMPOUNDED                7
    WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION TO A PATIENT SHALL PROVIDE THE PATIENT WITH                    8
    THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION:                                                            9
           (I) ANY SIDE EFFECTS, ADVERSE REACTIONS, CONTRAINDICATIONS,                   10
    PRECAUTIONS, AND WARNINGS ASSOCIATED WITH THE COMPOUNDED                             11
    WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION; AND                                                          12
           (II) IF A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION CONTAINS AN ACTIVE                13
    INGREDIENT THAT IS LISTED OR IS CLAIMED TO BE THE SAME AS AN ACTIVE                  14
    INGREDIENT IN A DRUG THAT IS APPROVED BY THE FDA, A SUMMARY OF THE                   15
    RISK INFORMATION DESCRIBED IN SUBSECTION (3)(b)(I) OF THIS SECTION THAT              16
    IS ON THE LABEL OF THE FDA-APPROVED DRUG.                                            17
          (4) Deceptive advertising.                                                     18
          (a) A PERSON SHALL NOT MAKE A FALSE OR MISLEADING CLAIM,                       19
    INCLUDING AN UNSUBSTANTIATED CLAIM, ABOUT A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS                   20
    MEDICATION WHEN THE PERSON IS ADVERTISING OR OTHERWISE PROMOTING THE                 21
    COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION.                                                   22
           (b) A CLAIM ABOUT A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION IS                      23
    CONSIDERED MISLEADING IF THE CLAIM DOES NOT INCLUDE:                                 24
           (I) A DISCLOSURE OF THE POTENTIAL SIDE EFFECTS, ADVERSE                       25
    REACTIONS, CONTRAINDICATIONS, PRECAUTIONS, AND WARNINGS ASSOCIATED                   26
    WITH ACTIVE INGREDIENTS IN THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION;                    27
           (II) A SUMMARY OF THE SPECIFIED RISK INFORMATION FOR AN ACTIVE                28
    INGREDIENT OF THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION THAT IS LISTED                   29
    OR CLAIMED TO BE THE SAME AS AN ACTIVE INGREDIENT IN AN FDA-APPROVED                 30
    DRUG, WHICH RISK INFORMATION IS CONTAINED ON THE LABEL OF THE                        31
    FDA-APPROVED DRUG;                                                                   32
           (III) A CLEAR, CONSPICUOUS STATEMENT THAT THE PRODUCT IS A                    33
    COMPOUNDED MEDICATION, HAS NOT BEEN APPROVED BY THE FDA AND HAS                      34
    NOT BEEN EVALUATED BY THE FDA FOR SAFETY OR EFFICACY; AND                            35
           (IV) A DISCLOSURE OF THE ENTITIES, SUCH AS SPECIFIC PHARMACIES                36
    AND OUTSOURCING FACILITIES, THAT ARE USED TO COMPOUND THE                            37
    COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION.                                                   38
          (5) Records and inspections.                                                   39
          (a) (I) A PERSON THAT SELLS, TRANSFERS, OR DISTRIBUTES                         40
    COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION SHALL MAINTAIN ALL RECORDS                         41
    RELATED TO THE ACQUISITION, EXAMINATION, AND TESTING OF THE BULK DRUG                42
    SUBSTANCES USED IN THE COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION FOR AT                      43
    LEAST TWO YEARS AFTER THE EXPIRATION DATE OF THE LAST LOT OF                         44
    COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION CONTAINING BULK DRUG                               45
    SUBSTANCES.                                                                          46
           (II) IF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL REQUESTS RECORDS FROM A PERSON                   47
    THAT SELLS, TRANSFERS, OR DISTRIBUTES COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS                         48
    MEDICATION, THE PERSON SHALL PROVIDE SUCH RECORDS TO THE ATTORNEY                    49
    GENERAL WITHIN ONE BUSINESS DAY AFTER RECEIVING THE REQUEST OR WITHIN                50
    ANOTHER REASONABLE TIME FRAME AS DETERMINED BY THE ATTORNEY                          51
    GENERAL BASED ON THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE REQUEST.                                   52
           (b) (I) TO DETERMINE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS SECTION, THE ATTORNEY               53
    GENERAL MAY INSPECT THE PREMISES OF A PERSON THAT ENGAGES IN THE                     54
    COMPOUNDING OF WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION, INCLUDING A DOMESTIC                          55
    SUPPLIER, WHOLESALER, REPACKAGER, OR OTHER PROVIDER OF BULK DRUG                     56
    SUBSTANCES USED FOR COMPOUNDING WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATIONS.                             57
           (II) A PERSON THAT REFUSES TO COMPLY WITH AN INSPECTION                       58
    CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (5)(b)(I) OF THIS SECTION IS IN                     59
    VIOLATION OF THIS SECTION.                                                           60
           (6) Enforcement.                                                              61
           (a) IF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL DETERMINES THAT A PERSON HAS                      62
    VIOLATED THIS SECTION, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY:                                     63
           (I) ASSESS A FINE IN THE AMOUNT OF UP TO ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS                 64
    PER COMPOUND PACKAGE UNIT OR VIAL OF A COMPOUNDED WEIGHT-LOSS                        65
    MEDICATION THAT IS SOLD, OFFERED FOR SALE, DISPENSED, TRANSFERRED,                   66
    DISTRIBUTED, ADVERTISED, OR PROMOTED IN VIOLATION OF THIS SECTION; OR                67
Page 342     Senate Journal-52nd Day-March 6, 2026


                        (II) PURSUE ANY OTHER REMEDY AVAILABLE UNDER THIS ARTICLE 1.                        1
                        (b) NOTWITHSTANDING SECTION 6-1-103, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL HAS                       2
                 EXCLUSIVE AUTHORITY TO ENFORCE THIS SECTION PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE                       3
                 1.                                                                                         4
                         (c) NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS ARTICLE 1,                         5
                 NOTHING IN THIS SECTION PROVIDES THE BASIS FOR, OR IS THE SUBJECT OF, A                    6
                 PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS SECTION.                                   7
                         (7) Applicability. THIS SECTION DOES NOT APPLY TO:                                 8
                         (a) THE COMPOUNDING OF A DRUG ADMINISTERED BY A PRACTITIONER                       9
                 AT AN ENTITY LICENSED PURSUANT TO SECTION 25-1.5-103 (1)(a)(I)(A);                        10
                         (b) A LONG-TERM CARE FACILITY, AS DEFINED IN SECTION 12-280-103                   11
                 (25); OR                                                                                  12
                         (c) THE COMPOUNDING OF A DRUG FOR ANIMAL USE.                                     13
                         SECTION 3. Applicability. This act applies to conduct occurring on                14
                 or after the effective date of this act.                                                  15
                         SECTION 4. Safety clause. The general assembly finds, determines,                 16
                 and declares that this act is necessary for the immediate preservation of the             17
                 public peace, health, or safety or for appropriations for the support and                 18
                 maintenance of the departments of the state and state institutions.".                     19

                                                                                                   26
                   Amend printed bill, strike everything below the enacting clause and substitute: 27
                                                                                                   28
                          "SECTION 1. In Colorado Revised Statutes, add 40-3-122 as follows:       29
                          40-3-122. Energy affordability - percentage-of-income payment            30
                   plan program - eligibility and participation - cost recovery - definitions -    31
                   rules.                                                                          32
                          (1) Definitions. AS USED IN THIS SECTION, UNLESS THE CONTEXT             33
                   OTHERWISE REQUIRES:                                                             34
                          (a) (I) "ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS" MEANS A UTILITY'S DIRECT COSTS FOR        35
                   LABOR, INCLUDING APPLICABLE BENEFIT LOADINGS, MATERIALS, AND OTHER              36
                   VERIFIABLE EXPENDITURES DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE ADMINISTRATION AND              37
                   OPERATION OF A PIPP PROGRAM.                                                    38
                          (II) ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS MUST NOT EXCEED TEN PERCENT OF THE             39
                   TOTAL AMOUNT OF THE FIXED CREDITS APPLIED TO CUSTOMER BILLS FOR                 40
                   CURRENT USAGE AND PRE-EXISTING ARREARAGES, OR TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS,             41
                   WHICHEVER AMOUNT IS GREATER.                                                    42
                          (b) "AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME" MEANS THE AMOUNT OF A              43
                   PARTICIPANT'S ANNUAL BILL THAT IS DEEMED AFFORDABLE BASED ON A                  44
                   PARTICIPANT'S ANNUAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME, AS DETERMINED PURSUANT TO                45
                   SUBSECTIONS (4)(b) AND (4)(c) OF THIS SECTION.                                  46
                          (c) "ARREARAGE" MEANS THE PAST-DUE BALANCE OWED BY A                     47
                   PARTICIPANT IN A PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM FOR                  48
                   UTILITY SERVICE, AS SHOWN ON THE MOST RECENT BILL RECEIVED BY THE               49
                   PARTICIPANT BEFORE THE PARTICIPANT ENROLLS IN THE PIPP PROGRAM.                 50
                          (d) (I) "FIXED CREDIT" MEANS AN ANNUAL BILL CREDIT THAT IS               51
                   CALCULATED BY A UTILITY AT THE BEGINNING OF A PARTICIPANT'S                     52
                   PARTICIPATION IN THE UTILITY'S PIPP PROGRAM EACH YEAR AND IS DELIVERED          53
                   AS AN EQUAL MONTHLY CREDIT ON THE PARTICIPANT'S MONTHLY UTILITY BILL.           54
                          (II) THE FIXED CREDIT IS EQUAL TO THE PARTICIPANT'S TOTAL                55
                   PROJECTED FULL ANNUAL BILL MINUS THE PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE                   56
                   PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT.                                                   57
                          (e) "FULL ANNUAL BILL" MEANS THE PROJECTED ELECTRICITY                   58
                   CONSUMPTION OF A PARTICIPANT IN ONE CALENDAR YEAR BILLED AT STANDARD            59
                   RESIDENTIAL RATES BEFORE ANY FIXED CREDIT AMOUNT OR OTHER CREDITS OR            60
                   DISCOUNTS ARE APPLIED TO THE BILL.                                              61
                          (f) "INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMER" HAS THE MEANING SET              62
                   FORTH IN SECTION 40-3-106 (1)(d)(II).                                           63
                          (g) "INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY" OR "UTILITY" MEANS A RETAIL                 64
                   ELECTRIC UTILITY OR A COMBINED RETAIL ELECTRIC AND GAS UTILITY IN THE           65
                   STATE THAT IS REGULATED BY THE COMMISSION AND IS NOT A COOPERATIVE              66
                   ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION OR A MUNICIPALLY OWNED UTILITY.                            67
Senate Journal-58th Day-March 12, 2026                                             Page 381


           (h) "PARTICIPANT" MEANS AN INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMER                        1
    WHO IS APPROVED FOR PARTICIPATION IN A UTILITY'S PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME                      2
    PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM.                                                                      3
           (i) "PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM" OR "PIPP                            4
    PROGRAM" MEANS A PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM FOR RESIDENTIAL PARTICIPANTS                         5
    IN WHICH A PARTICIPANT'S UTILITY BILL DOES NOT EXCEED AN AFFORDABLE                        6
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME.                                                                      7
           (j) "PIPP CHARGE" MEANS A FEE CHARGED TO AN INVESTOR-OWNED                          8
    UTILITY'S CUSTOMERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH SUBSECTION (7) OF THIS SECTION                      9
    TO RECOVER COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE UTILITY'S PIPP PROGRAM.                              10
           (k)    "UNAFFORDABLE PORTION" MEANS THE AMOUNT OF A                                11
    PARTICIPANT'S ESTIMATED FULL ANNUAL BILL THAT EXCEEDS THE AFFORDABLE                      12
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAID BY THE PARTICIPANT.                                             13
             (2) Percentage-of-income payment plan program.                                   14
             (a)       AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL ESTABLISH A                            15
    PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM FOR RESIDENTIAL                                 16
    INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMERS.                                                       17
             (b) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL USE CONSISTENT NAMING FOR                    18
    THE PIPP PROGRAM IN TARIFFS, RATES, CUSTOMER COMMUNICATIONS, AND BILL                     19
    S T A T E M E N T S , W H I C H N A M E M U S T I N C L U D E T H E WO R D S              20
    "PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM".                                              21
             (c) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL PUBLISH THE FOLLOWING                        22
    INFORMATION RELATED TO THE PIPP PROGRAM ON THE UTILITY'S PUBLIC                           23
    WEBSITE:                                                                                  24
             (I) THE INCOME ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR THE PIPP PROGRAM;                        25
             (II) AN EXPLANATION OF WHAT THE PIPP PROGRAM DOES;                               26
             (III) THE APPLICATION AND ENROLLMENT PROCESSES;                                  27
             (IV) AN ESTIMATED TIME FRAME FOR WHEN AN APPLICANT WILL                          28
    RECEIVE NOTICE OF THEIR ACCEPTANCE INTO OR DENIAL FROM THE PIPP                           29
    PROGRAM;                                                                                  30
             (V) AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME AMOUNTS FOR DIFFERENT                        31
    TYPES OF CUSTOMERS, AS DESCRIBED IN SUBSECTION (4) OF THIS SECTION;                       32
             (VI) PIPP CHARGE AMOUNTS; AND                                                    33
             (VII) THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR THE UTILITY'S PIPP PROGRAM.                   34
             (3) Eligibility and participation.                                               35
             (a) AN INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMER IS ELIGIBLE TO                          36
    PARTICIPATE IN THE PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM IF THE                       37
    CUSTOMER:                                                                                 38
             (I) MEETS THE INCOME ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA, AS DETERMINED BY THE                  39
    COMMISSION BY ORDER OR BY RULE;                                                           40
             (II) EITHER:                                                                     41
             (A) SUBMITS AN APPLICATION TO THE INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY TO                      42
    PARTICIPATE IN THE PIPP PROGRAM; OR                                                       43
             (B) IS REFERRED BY ANOTHER INCOME-ELIGIBLE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM                    44
    OFFERED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES, CREATED IN SECTION                           45
    26-1-105; THE COLORADO ENERGY OFFICE, CREATED IN SECTION 24-38.5-101;                     46
    THE ORGANIZATION DEFINED IN SECTION 40-8.7-103 (4); OR OTHER ENERGY                       47
    ASSISTANCE PROGRAM APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION; AND                                        48
             (III) LIVES IN THE SERVICE AREA OF AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY THAT                49
    HAS ESTABLISHED A PIPP PROGRAM.                                                           50
             (b) (I) AN APPLICANT THAT SUBMITS A PIPP PROGRAM APPLICATION TO                  51
    AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY MAY SUBMIT DOCUMENTATION WITH THE                               52
    APPLICATION VERIFYING THAT THE APPLICANT MEETS THE INCOME ELIGIBILITY                     53
    CRITERIA, INCLUDING:                                                                      54
           (A) DOCUMENTATION THAT THE APPLICANT IS ENROLLED IN ANOTHER                        55
    INCOME-ELIGIBLE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM OFFERED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF                           56
    HUMAN SERVICES, CREATED IN SECTION 26-1-105; THE COLORADO ENERGY                          57
    OFFICE, CREATED IN SECTION 24-38.5-101; THE ORGANIZATION DEFINED IN                       58
    SECTION 40-8.7-103 (4); OR OTHER ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM APPROVED                       59
    BY THE COMMISSION; OR                                                                     60
           (B) A SELF-ATTESTATION, THROUGH A PROCESS ESTABLISHED BY THE                       61
    UTILITY FOR THE PIPP PROGRAM, OF THE APPLICANT'S INCOME ELIGIBILITY.                      62
           (II) IF AN APPLICANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME IS ZERO DOLLARS, THE                       63
    UTILITY MAY ESTABLISH A PROCESS THAT VERIFIES THE APPLICANT'S                             64
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME ON A MORE FREQUENT THAN ANNUAL BASIS.                                    65
           (c) AN APPLICANT IS NOT REQUIRED TO MAKE A PAYMENT ON THE                          66
    APPLICANT'S ACCOUNT AS A CONDITION OF ACCEPTANCE INTO A PIPP PROGRAM.                     67
Page 382   Senate Journal-58th Day-March 12, 2026


                      (d) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL ESTABLISH APPLICATION AND        1
               PARTICIPATION PROCEDURES THAT ARE EFFICIENT, AVAILABLE TO APPLICANTS        2
               IN PLAIN LANGUAGE, AND INTENDED TO MAXIMIZE PARTICIPATION IN THE            3
               UTILITY'S PIPP PROGRAM.                                                     4
                      (e) (I) WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER RECEIVING A PIPP PROGRAM            5
               APPLICATION FROM AN INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMER, AN                   6
               INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL APPROVE OR DENY THE INCOME-QUALIFIED           7
               UTILITY CUSTOMER'S APPLICATION.                                             8
                      (II) IF THE INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY APPROVES AN INCOME-QUALIFIED      9
               UTILITY CUSTOMER'S APPLICATION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PIPP PROGRAM,      10
               THE UTILITY SHALL PROVIDE AN EXPLANATION OF THE PIPP PROGRAM BENEFITS,     11
               INCLUDING:                                                                 12
                      (A) THE PARTICIPANT'S ESTIMATED FULL ANNUAL BILL AMOUNT;            13
                      (B) THE PARTICIPANT'S FIXED CREDIT AMOUNT;                          14
                      (C) THE AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME FOR WHICH THE               15
               PARTICIPANT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR PAYING, LISTED AS BOTH A PERCENTAGE AND     16
               AN ESTIMATED MONTHLY AMOUNT; AND                                           17
                      (D) A COPY OF THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION IN THE      18
               PIPP PROGRAM.                                                              19
                      (III) IF THE INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY DENIES AN APPLICANT'S           20
               APPLICATION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PIPP PROGRAM, THE UTILITY SHALL       21
               PROVIDE THE APPLICANT AN EXPLANATION FOR THE DENIAL AND, IF THE REASON     22
               FOR THE DENIAL WAS BASED ON THE UTILITY'S VERIFICATION OF THE              23
               APPLICANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME IN ACCORDANCE WITH SUBSECTION (3)(b) OF       24
               THIS SECTION, THE DEPARTMENT, AGENCY, OR ORGANIZATION THAT THE             25
               UTILITY CONTACTED TO VERIFY THE APPLICANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME.              26
                      (IV) IF AN INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMER IS ACCEPTED INTO       27
               THE PIPP PROGRAM, THE CUSTOMER SHALL REMAIN QUALIFIED FOR THE PIPP         28
               PROGRAM FOR TWO PROGRAM YEARS AFTER THE DATE ON WHICH THE                  29
               CUSTOMER IS ACCEPTED INTO THE PROGRAM.                                     30
                      (f) (I) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ESTABLISHING   31
               AND ADMINISTERING THE PROCESS FOR INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY CUSTOMERS       32
               TO APPLY FOR PARTICIPATION AND MAINTAINING ENROLLMENT IN THE PIPP          33
               PROGRAM.                                                                   34
                      (II) A PARTICIPANT MAY REMAIN ENROLLED IN A UTILITY'S PIPP          35
               PROGRAM IF THE PARTICIPANT MOVES WITHIN THE SAME UTILITY SERVICE           36
               TERRITORY WITHOUT REAPPLYING FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PIPP PROGRAM,        37
               AND THE PARTICIPANT SHALL NOTIFY THE UTILITY OF THE PARTICIPANT'S          38
               CHANGE OF ADDRESS AND NEW ACCOUNT NUMBER.                                  39
                      (III) IF A PARTICIPANT MOVES OUTSIDE OF A UTILITY'S SERVICE         40
               TERRITORY, THE PARTICIPANT IS NO LONGER ELIGIBLE FOR THE UTILITY'S PIPP    41
               PROGRAM AND THE UTILITY SHALL SEND NOTICE TO THE PARTICIPANT THAT THE      42
               PARTICIPANT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR AND ENROLLMENT IN THE PIPP PROGRAM HAS       43
               ENDED.                                                                     44
                      (g) IF A PARTICIPANT MAKES PARTIAL OR LATE PAYMENTS ON THEIR        45
               UTILITY BILL, THE INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL NOT TERMINATE THE           46
               PARTICIPANT'S PARTICIPATION IN THE PIPP PROGRAM SOLELY FOR THAT            47
               REASON. HOWEVER, THE UTILITY MAY PURSUE COLLECTION EFFORTS FOR THE         48
               UNPAID AMOUNTS.                                                            49
                      (4) Affordable percentage of income calculation.                    50
                      (a) (I) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL ESTIMATE A PARTICIPANT'S    51
               FULL ANNUAL BILL IN ORDER TO DETERMINE A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE          52
               PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH SUBSECTIONS (4)(b)         53
               AND (4)(c) OF THIS SECTION.                                                54
                      (II) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL INCLUDE THE DIFFERENCE         55
               BETWEEN A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT AND        56
               THE PROJECTED FULL ANNUAL BILL ON THE PARTICIPANT'S UTILITY BILL AS A      57
               FIXED CREDIT.                                                              58
                      (III) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY MAY ADJUST THE FIXED CREDIT         59
               AMOUNT IF RESIDENTIAL RATES FOR ELECTRICITY SIGNIFICANTLY CHANGE FROM      60
               THE RATE USED TO ESTIMATE THE PARTICIPANT'S FULL ANNUAL BILL OR IF THE     61
               PARTICIPANT'S ACTUAL BILL AMOUNT VARIES BY TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT OR          62
               MORE FROM THE PARTICIPANT'S ESTIMATED FULL ANNUAL BILL.                    63
                      (b) UNLESS OTHERWISE DETERMINED BY THE COMMISSION BY ORDER          64
               OR BY RULE, IF A PARTICIPANT'S ANNUAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME IS ABOVE ZERO       65
               DOLLARS, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME MUST NOT          66
               EXCEED THE APPLICABLE PERCENTAGE OF HOUSEHOLD INCOME AS FOLLOWS:           67
Senate Journal-58th Day-March 12, 2026                                        Page 383


             (I) FOR UTILITIES WITH FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND CUSTOMERS OR                    1
    FEWER:                                                                                2
           (A) FOR ELECTRIC ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE ELECTRICITY AS THE PRIMARY                 3
    HEATING FUEL, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME                         4
    PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN SIX PERCENT OF THE PARTICIPANT'S                     5
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME;                                                                     6
           (B) FOR ELECTRIC ACCOUNTS THAT DO NOT HAVE ELECTRICITY AS THE                  7
    PRIMARY HEATING FUEL, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME                 8
    PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN THREE PERCENT OF THE PARTICIPANT'S                   9
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME;                                                                    10
           (C) FOR ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE BOTH NATURAL GAS SERVICE AND                       11
    ELECTRIC SERVICE FROM A SINGLE UTILITY, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE                   12
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN FIVE PERCENT                   13
    OF THE PARTICIPANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME; OR                                            14
           (D) FOR ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE NEITHER ELECTRICITY NOR NATURAL                    15
    GAS AS A PRIMARY HEATING SOURCE, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE                          16
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN FIVE PERCENT                   17
    OF THE PARTICIPANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME; AND                                           18
           (II) FOR UTILITIES WITH MORE THAN FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND                       19
    CUSTOMERS:                                                                           20
           (A) FOR ELECTRIC ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE ELECTRICITY AS THE PRIMARY                21
    HEATING FUEL, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME                        22
    PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN FOUR PERCENT OF THE PARTICIPANT'S                   23
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME;                                                                    24
           (B) FOR ELECTRIC ACCOUNTS THAT DO NOT HAVE ELECTRICITY AS THE                 25
    PRIMARY HEATING FUEL, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME                26
    PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN TWO PERCENT OF THE PARTICIPANT'S                    27
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME;                                                                    28
           (C) FOR ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE BOTH NATURAL GAS SERVICE AND                       29
    ELECTRIC SERVICE FROM A SINGLE UTILITY, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE                   30
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN FIVE PERCENT                   31
    OF THE PARTICIPANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME; OR                                            32
           (D) FOR ACCOUNTS THAT HAVE NEITHER ELECTRICITY NOR NATURAL                    33
    GAS AS A PRIMARY HEATING SOURCE, A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE                          34
    PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE GREATER THAN FIVE PERCENT                   35
    OF THE PARTICIPANT'S HOUSEHOLD INCOME.                                               36
           (c) IF A PARTICIPANT'S ANNUAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME IS ZERO DOLLARS,               37
    A PARTICIPANT'S AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME MUST NOT EXCEED THE                  38
    APPLICABLE PERCENTAGE OF HOUSEHOLD INCOME AS FOLLOWS:                                39
           (I) FOR AN ELECTRIC HEATING ACCOUNT, THE PARTICIPANT'S                        40
    AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE MORE THAN                        41
    TWENTY DOLLARS PER MONTH; OR                                                         42
           (II) FOR AN ELECTRIC NONHEATING ACCOUNT, THE PARTICIPANT'S                    43
    AFFORDABLE PERCENTAGE OF INCOME PAYMENT MUST NOT BE MORE THAN TEN                    44
    DOLLARS PER MONTH.                                                                   45
           (5) Arrearage credits.                                                        46
           (a) (I) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL APPLY ARREARAGE CREDITS               47
    TO A PARTICIPANT'S ARREARAGES THAT EXISTED BEFORE THE PARTICIPANT                    48
    APPLIED FOR THE PIPP PROGRAM.                                                        49
           (II) ARREARAGE CREDITS MUST BE ESTABLISHED AND APPLIED TO A                   50
    PARTICIPANT'S UTILITY BILL IN AN AMOUNT SUFFICIENT TO REDUCE, WHEN                   51
    COMBINED WITH ANY REQUIRED PAYMENTS FROM THE PARTICIPANT, THE                        52
    PARTICIPANT'S ARREARAGES TO ZERO DOLLARS OVER A PERIOD OF NOT LESS                   53
    THAN ONE MONTH AND NOT MORE THAN TWENTY-FOUR MONTHS.                                 54
           (b) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY MAY CONDITION THE APPLICATION                   55
    OF ARREARAGE CREDITS ON THE FOLLOWING:                                               56
           (I) A PARTICIPANT'S TIMELY PAYMENT OF BILLS FOR CURRENT USAGE;                57
    OR                                                                                   58
           (II) A PARTICIPANT'S PAYMENT TOWARD PREEXISTING ARREARAGES,                   59
    EXCEPT THAT THE TOTAL DOLLAR AMOUNT OF THE PAYMENT REQUIRED BY THE                   60
    UTILITY MUST NOT EXCEED ONE PERCENT OF THE PARTICIPANT'S ANNUAL                      61
    HOUSEHOLD INCOME.                                                                    62
           (c) IF A PARTICIPANT'S ENROLLMENT IN THE PIPP PROGRAM ENDS FOR                63
    ANY REASON PRIOR TO THE FORGIVENESS OF ALL ARREARAGES, ANY REMAINING                 64
    ARREARAGES BECOME DUE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE UTILITY'S CURRENT                       65
    TARIFF FILED WITH THE COMMISSION AT THE TIME OF THE TERMINATION.                     66
           (d) WHILE A PARTICIPANT IS ENROLLED IN A UTILITY'S PIPP PROGRAM,              67
Page 384   Senate Journal-58th Day-March 12, 2026


               THE UTILITY SHALL NOT TERMINATE THE PARTICIPANT'S SERVICE FOR                        1
               NONPAYMENT OF THE ARREARAGES.                                                        2
                      (e) A PARTICIPANT MAY RECEIVE ARREARAGE CREDITS PURSUANT TO                   3
               THIS SECTION REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE PARTICIPANT RECEIVES A CREDIT                 4
               TOWARD A UTILITY BILL FOR CURRENT USAGE.                                             5
                      (6) Participation in other assistance programs.                               6
                      (a) THIS SECTION DOES NOT PROHIBIT AN INCOME-QUALIFIED UTILITY                7
               CUSTOMER FROM PARTICIPATING IN OTHER ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS                      8
               WHILE ENROLLED IN A PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM.                       9
                      (b) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY MAY APPLY ENERGY ASSISTANCE                    10
               GRANTS PROVIDED TO A PARTICIPANT TO THE DOLLAR VALUE OF THE FIXED                   11
               CREDITS PROVIDED TO THE PARTICIPANT TO COVER THE UNAFFORDABLE                       12
               PORTION OF THE PARTICIPANT'S UTILITY BILL IN A MANNER DETERMINED BY THE             13
               COMMISSION BY RULE.                                                                 14
                      (7) Cost recovery.                                                           15
                      (a)      A N INVESTOR - OWNED UTILITY MAY RECOVER                            16
               PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME PAYMENT PLAN PROGRAM COSTS THROUGH A PIPP                      17
               CHARGE ON THE UTILITY'S CUSTOMERS, AS APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION.                   18
                      (b) IF AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY IMPOSES A PIPP CHARGE, THE                  19
               INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL:                                                       20
                      (I) ASSESS THE PIPP CHARGE AS A SEPARATE LINE ITEM ON EVERY                  21
               CUSTOMER'S MONTHLY BILL AND IDENTIFY THE CHARGE AS A "PIPP CHARGE";                 22
                      (II) COLLECT THE MONTHLY PIPP CHARGE IN THE SAME MANNER AS ALL               23
               OTHER CHARGES AND FEES ARE COLLECTED FROM A CUSTOMER;                               24
                      (III) STATE THE AMOUNT OF THE PIPP CHARGE, WHICH MUST BE                     25
               APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION; AND                                                     26
                      (IV) INCLUDE THE AMOUNT OF PIPP CHARGES COLLECTED FROM A                     27
               UTILITY'S CUSTOMERS ON THE UTILITY'S TARIFF SHEET FILED WITH THE                    28
               COMMISSION.                                                                         29
                      (c) IF AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY IMPOSES A PIPP CHARGE, THE                  30
               UTILITY IS ENCOURAGED TO ANNUALLY CONTRIBUTE SHAREHOLDER PROFITS TO                 31
               THE PIPP PROGRAM. ANY AMOUNT CONTRIBUTED BY THE UTILITY IS NOT TO BE                32
               DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY RECOVERED FROM CUSTOMERS.                                    33
                      (d) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY MUST USE THE REVENUE GENERATED                 34
               FROM THE PIPP CHARGE PLUS ANY AMOUNT CONTRIBUTED BY THE UTILITY                     35
               PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (7)(c) OF THIS SECTION ONLY FOR THE FOLLOWING                36
               PURPOSES:                                                                           37
                      (I) TO PROVIDE CREDITS OR DISCOUNTS TO PARTICIPANTS APPLIED                  38
               AGAINST THE PARTICIPANTS' BILL FOR CURRENT USAGE;                                   39
                      (II) TO PROVIDE CREDITS TO PARTICIPANTS FOR THE PARTICIPANTS'                40
               ARREARAGES;                                                                         41
                      (III) TO COVER ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS OF IMPLEMENTING AND                      42
               ADMINISTERING THE PIPP PROGRAM; AND                                                 43
                      (IV) TO COVER PIPP PROGRAM EVALUATION COSTS REQUIRED BY THE                  44
               COMMISSION.                                                                         45
                      (e) THE COMMISSION SHALL DETERMINE BY RULE THE AMOUNT OF THE                 46
               PIPP CHARGE AND PROCEDURES BY WHICH A UTILITY MAY APPLY TO INCREASE                 47
               OR DECREASE THE MONTHLY PIPP CHARGE.                                                48
                      (f) (I) AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY SHALL TRACK AND ANNUALLY                   49
               REPORT THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION TO THE COMMISSION:                                 50
                      (A) THE PIPP CHARGE REVENUE COLLECTED BY THE UTILITY;                        51
                      (B) THE PIPP CHARGE UTILITY CONTRIBUTION AMOUNT DESCRIBED IN                 52
               SUBSECTION (7)(c) OF THIS SECTION;                                                  53
                      (C) ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH IMPLEMENTING AND                    54
               ADMINISTERING THE PIPP PROGRAM;                                                     55
                      (D) THE AMOUNT OF FIXED CREDITS PROVIDED TO PARTICIPANTS IN THE              56
               PIPP PROGRAM; AND                                                                   57
                      (E) THE AMOUNT OF ARREARAGE CREDITS PROVIDED TO PARTICIPANTS                 58
               IN THE PIPP PROGRAM.                                                                59
                      (II) THE COMMISSION SHALL REPORT THE INFORMATION REPORTED BY                 60
               AN INVESTOR-OWNED UTILITY PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (7)(f)(I) OF THIS                  61
               SECTION IN THE COMMISSION'S ANNUAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS                           62
               ESTABLISHED BY THE COMMISSION BY RULE.                                              63
                      (8) Rules. THE COMMISSION SHALL ADOPT ANY RULES NECESSARY TO                 64
               IMPLEMENT AND ENFORCE THIS SECTION.                                                 65

              favorable recommendation.                                                                  19
                                                                                                         20
                   Amend printed bill, strike everything below the enacting clause and substitute:       21
                            "SECTION 1. Legislative declaration. (1) The general assembly                22
                   finds and declares that:                                                              23
                            (a) The Colorado Measures of Academic Success assessments place an           24
                   undue burden on students and educators across the state;                              25
                            (b) According to the department of education, each student in grades 3       26
                   through 8 spends up to eleven hours each year completing these statewide              27
                   assessments;                                                                          28
                            (c) The amount of time required to administer statewide assessments          29
                   does not include additional instructional time lost to test preparation, educator     30
                   training, make-up testing, or modified school schedules, which disrupt multiple       31
                   weeks of academic instruction for students and staff;                                 32
                            (d) Statewide assessments are administered to satisfy federal                33
                   requirements. Federal law permits flexibility in the state's assessments to meet      34
                   those requirements.                                                                   35
                            (e) Colorado administers more statewide testing than is required under       36
                   federal law;                                                                          37
                            (f) Statewide assessments are summative in nature and intended to            38
                   produce comparable data for accountability, but the delayed return of results         39
                   limits the ability of educators to use that data to inform instruction for the tested 40
                   students;                                                                             41
                            (g) In addition to statewide assessments, students in Colorado complete      42
                   multiple other locally administered assessments;                                      43
                            (h) Locally administered assessments typically return results quicker        44
                   and provide educators with timely data that can be used to support instruction        45
                   and student mastery of the assessed subjects;                                         46
                            (i) Reducing statewide assessments would return meaningful                   47
                   instructional time to students and educators and allow greater reliance on            48
                   timely, actionable assessment data already collected by local education               49
                   providers;                                                                            50
                            (j) Furthermore, reducing the length of statewide assessments provides       51
                   a cost savings to the state, which spends approximately $20 million annually to       52
                   develop and administer statewide assessments; and                                     53
                            (k) It is necessary to convene a working group to develop                    54
                   recommendations to reduce the amount of time required for statewide                   55
                   assessments used to satisfy federal requirements.                                     56
                            SECTION 2. In Colorado Revised Statutes, add 22-7-1006.2 as                  57
                   follows:                                                                              58
                            22-7-1006.2. State assessments modifications - working group -               59
                   report - definitions - repeal.                                                        60
                            (1) AS USED IN THIS SECTION, UNLESS THE CONTEXT OTHERWISE                    61
                   REQUIRES:                                                                             62
                            (a) "DEPARTMENT" MEANS THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION CREATED                   63
                   AND EXISTING PURSUANT TO SECTION 24-1-115.                                            64
                            (b) "RURAL SCHOOL DISTRICT" MEANS A SCHOOL DISTRICT IN                       65
                   COLORADO THAT THE DEPARTMENT DETERMINES IS RURAL BASED ON THE                         66
                   GEOGRAPHIC SIZE OF THE SCHOOL DISTRICT AND THE DISTANCE OF THE SCHOOL                 67
Senate Journal-63rd Day-March 17, 2026                                       Page 419


    DISTRICT FROM THE NEAREST LARGE URBANIZED AREA.                                      1
           (c) "SMALL RURAL SCHOOL DISTRICT" MEANS A RURAL SCHOOL                        2
    DISTRICT THAT ENROLLS FEWER THAN ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED STUDENTS                   3
    IN KINDERGARTEN THROUGH TWELFTH GRADE.                                               4
           (d)     "WORKING GROUP" MEANS THE STATE ASSESSMENTS                           5
    MODIFICATIONS WORKING GROUP CREATED AND EXISTING PURSUANT TO                         6
    SUBSECTION (2) OF THIS SECTION.                                                      7
           (2) (a) THERE IS CREATED THE STATE ASSESSMENTS MODIFICATIONS                  8
    WORKING GROUP.                                                                       9
           (b) THE WORKING GROUP IS:                                                    10
           (I) THE FOLLOWING MEMBERS, APPOINTED BY THE CHAIR OF THE                     11
    SENATE EDUCATION COMMITTEE, OR ANY SUCCESSOR COMMITTEE:                             12

    THE ADVICE OF A STATEWIDE ASSOCIATION THAT REPRESENTS SCHOOL DISTRICT               23

           (E) A CHARTER SCHOOL TEACHER, APPOINTED WITH THE ADVICE OF A                 25
    STATEWIDE ASSOCIATION THAT ADVOCATES FOR CHARTER SCHOOLS; AND                       26
           (II) THE FOLLOWING MEMBERS, APPOINTED BY THE CHAIR OF THE HOUSE              27
    EDUCATION COMMITTEE, OR ANY SUCCESSOR COMMITTEE:                                    28
           (A) TWO INDIVIDUALS, EACH OF WHOM IS EITHER A TEACHER EMPLOYED               29

                                                                                                      57
                           "SECTION 1. Legislative declaration. (1) The general assembly              58
                   finds and declares that:                                                           59
                           (a) On December 18, 2025, the air quality control commission in the        60
                   department of public health and environment adopted Regulation Number 31,          61
                   "Control of Methane Emissions from Municipal Solid Waste Landfills", 5 CCR         62
                   1001-35, to reduce methane emissions and other air pollutants from municipal       63
                   solid waste landfills;                                                             64
                           (b) Regulation Number 31 requires municipal solid waste landfills to       65
                   reduce methane emissions through the installation and operation of gas             66
                   collection and control systems and improved monitoring and gas management,         67
Senate Journal-91st Day-April 14, 2026                                                    Page 657


    thereby supporting cleaner air and lowering greenhouse gas emissions; and                         1
            (c) Compliance with Regulation Number 31 may impose a financial                           2
    burden on some entities that own or operate municipal solid waste landfills.                      3
            (2) The general assembly further finds and declares that:                                 4
            (a) The community impact cash fund was created in section 25-7-129,                       5
    Colorado Revised Statutes, to provide financial assistance for environmental                      6
    mitigation projects through the environmental justice grant program using air                     7
    quality-related penalty revenue. The community impact cash fund is an existing                    8
    source of state financial assistance intended to address impacts of air and water                 9
    quality to local communities and infrastructures.                                                10
            (b) The local government mineral impact fund, created in section                         11
    34-63-102 (5), Colorado Revised Statutes, consists of money that is distributed                  12
    by the executive director of the department of local affairs to counties, federal                13
    mineral lease districts, and municipalities in accordance with guidelines                        14
    established by the executive director in consultation with the energy impact                     15
    assistance advisory committee;                                                                   16
            (c) It is the intent of the general assembly that money in the community                 17
    impact cash fund and local government mineral impact fund may be used to                         18
    assist entities in complying with Regulation Number 31;                                          19
            (d) In determining any financial assistance for municipal solid waste                    20
    landfill methane emission reduction projects, priority should be given to                        21
    municipal solid waste landfills that are owned or operated by local governments                  22

                 Amend printed bill, strike everything below the enacting clause and substitute:        8
                                                                                                        9
                          "SECTION 1. Legislative declaration. (1) The general assembly                10
                 finds that:                                                                           11
                          (a) States across the country have enacted prison population                 12
                 management measures that recognize that overcrowded prison facilities are a           13
                 threat to the health and safety of staff and inmates;                                 14
                          (b) It is universally recognized that ensuring systematic and operational    15
                 efficiencies can effectively manage prison populations without compromising           16
                 public safety;                                                                        17
                          (c) In 2018, the Colorado general assembly unanimously adopted prison        18
                 population management measures that trigger specific actions when the                 19
                 department of corrections' prison bed vacancy rate falls below a specified level      20
                 for 30 consecutive days;                                                              21
                          (d) On August 16, 2025, the department of corrections' prison bed            22
                 vacancy rate fell to a level that triggered the prison population management          23
                 measures for the first time; and                                                      24
                          (e) The implementation of current prison population management               25
                 measures has not made an impact on prison overcrowding in Colorado. There             26
                 is limited data available to assess the reasons for this lack of impact since there   27
                 is no data reporting required by state law on the implementation of the               28
                 mandated prison population management measures. However, there is clearly             29
                 the potential for impact because reliable data indicates that a significant number    30
                 of inmates are eligible for placement in the community through community              31
                 corrections boards, and roughly 4,600 inmates are past their parole eligibility       32
                 date.                                                                                 33
                          (2) Therefore, the general assembly declares that revising Colorado's        34
                 existing prison population management measures is necessary in order to               35
                 address operational inefficiencies, obtain necessary data, and increase               36
                 transparency and accountability, and that the efficient management of prison          37
                 populations is a matter of ongoing concern for correctional staff and inmates.        38
                          SECTION 2. In Colorado Revised Statutes, amend 17-1-119.7 as                 39

                                                                                                            39
HB26-1071 by Representative(s) Mauro and Duran; also Senator(s) Cutter--Concerning allowing a               40
            local government to locate an automated vehicle identification system on an interstate          41
            highway.                                                                                        42
                                                                                                            43
              Amendment No. 1(L.006), by Senator Cutter.                                                    44
                   Amend reengrossed bill, page 2, after line 1 insert:                                     45
                                                                                                            46
                            "SECTION 1. Legislative declaration. (1) The general assembly                   47
                   finds and declares that:                                                                 48
                            (a) Municipalities have primary response authority for traffic                  49
                   enforcement on portions of federal interstates located in their jurisdiction             50
                   pursuant to section 43-2-135 (1)(g), Colorado Revised Statutes;                          51
                            (b) It is dangerous to conduct in-person traffic enforcement on interstate      52
                   highways, and municipalities expend significant resources responding to traffic          53
                   incidents on federal interstates;                                                        54
                            (c) Automated vehicle identification systems, referred to in this section       55
                   as "AVIS", are a safe and effective way to conduct traffic enforcement that              56
                   municipalities have been utilizing for at least 30 years;                                57
                            (d) In 1997, the general assembly adopted the first state law regarding         58
                   utilization of AVIS throughout Colorado. The law has been amended from time              59
                   to time but has remained in effect since that time.                                      60
                            (e) Federal prohibitions on masking convictions for traffic control             61
                   violations by commercial driver's license holders pursuant to 49 CFR 384.226             62
                   have never been implicated by the use of AVIS in the United States;                      63
                            (f) Federal masking is not implicated by AVIS because AVIS violations           64
                   result in administrative citations and penalties imposed on the vehicle owner,           65
                   not traffic control convictions, as that term is used in 49 CFR 384.226, imposed         66
                   on the driver;                                                                           67
Page 768    Senate Journal-97th Day-April 20, 2026


                         (g) Federal masking is only implicated where the identity of the driver        1
                is known, a conviction is obtained, and a deliberate decision is made not to            2
                place the conviction on the driving record;                                             3
                         (h) AVIS are separate and distinct from automated license plate readers        4
                in that AVIS do not continuously capture data for every passing vehicle and             5
                instead only activate and capture data when certain traffic violations occur;           6
                         (i) Under section 42-4-110.5 (7)(b), Colorado Revised Statutes,                7
                photographs or videos collected by AVIS are confidential and exempt from                8
                disclosure and inspection under the "Colorado Open Records Act"; and                    9
                         (j) Under section 24-74-103, Colorado Revised Statutes, state and             10
                political subdivision employees are prohibited from disclosing personal                11
                identifying information, which includes data from AVIS, for the purpose of             12
                investigating for, participating in, cooperating with, or assisting in federal         13
                immigration enforcement.                                                               14
                         (2) Therefore, the general assembly expressly declares that AVIS are          15
                a safe, effective, and highly regulated tool that has been successfully used solely    16

    COMMITMENT PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (1) OF THIS SECTION.                               17
           (4) (a) IF THE COURT DOES NOT DENY THE REQUEST FOR TERMINATION                18
    WITHOUT A HEARING, THE COURT SHALL PERMIT THE COUNTY ATTORNEY AND                    19
    THE DISTRICT ATTORNEY WHO ORIGINALLY SOUGHT CIVIL COMMITMENT OR                      20
    ENHANCED PROTECTIVE PLACEMENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 16-8.5-118                         21
    FOURTEEN DAYS TO OBJECT TO TERMINATION OR REQUEST AN OPPORTUNITY TO                  22
    CONDUCT AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATION BY AN EXPERT OF THE COUNTY                         23
    ATTORNEY'S OR DISTRICT ATTORNEY'S OWN CHOOSING AND EXPENSE.                          24
           (b) IF NEITHER THE COUNTY ATTORNEY NOR THE DISTRICT ATTORNEY                  25
    OBJECT OR REQUEST AN OPPORTUNITY TO REQUEST AN INDEPENDENT                           26
    EVALUATION, THE COURT SHALL TERMINATE THE RESPONDENT'S CIVIL                         27
    COMMITMENT.                                                                          28
           (c) IF EITHER THE COUNTY ATTORNEY OR THE DISTRICT ATTORNEY                    29
    REQUEST AN OPPORTUNITY TO CONDUCT AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATION, THE                     30
    COURT SHALL GRANT THAT REQUEST, ORDER THE RESPONDENT TO COMPLY WITH                  31
    THE EVALUATION, AND PERMIT THE COUNTY ATTORNEY OR DISTRICT ATTORNEY                  32
    A REASONABLE PERIOD OF TIME TO IDENTIFY AN EXPERT, CONDUCT THE                       33
    EVALUATION, AND ISSUE A REPORT. IF BOTH THE COUNTY ATTORNEY AND                      34
    DISTRICT ATTORNEY REQUEST AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATION, THE COURT                       35
    SHALL TREAT THE REQUEST AS A JOINT REQUEST FOR A SINGLE INDEPENDENT                  36
    EVALUATION.                                                                          37
           (d) IF THE RESPONDENT DOES NOT COOPERATE WITH THE EVALUATION,                 38
    THE COURT MAY GRANT ADDITIONAL TIME OR DENY THE RESPONDENT'S                         39
    REQUEST FOR TERMINATION.                                                             40
           (e) UPON RECEIPT OF THE INDEPENDENT EVALUATION REPORT, THE                    41
    COUNTY ATTORNEY OR DISTRICT ATTORNEY MUST PROVIDE A COPY TO                          42
    RESPONDENT'S COUNSEL AND THE COURT WITHIN FOURTEEN DAYS.                             43
           (f) IF NEITHER THE COUNTY ATTORNEY NOR DISTRICT ATTORNEY OBJECT               44
    WITHIN THE TIME PERMITTED BY THE COURT, THE COURT SHALL TERMINATE THE                45
    RESPONDENT'S CIVIL COMMITMENT.                                                       46
           (5) (a) IF EITHER THE COUNTY ATTORNEY OR DISTRICT ATTORNEY                    47
    TIMELY OBJECTS, THE COURT SHALL, AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, BRING THE                   48
    RESPONDENT BEFORE THE COURT, ENSURE THE RESPONDENT AND THE                           49
    RESPONDENT'S COUNSEL RECEIVED A COPY OF THE REPORT, AND ADVISE THE                   50

    PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (1) OF THIS SECTION.                                          54

    COURT SHALL SCHEDULE THE TRIAL TO BEGIN WITHIN THIRTY-FIVE DAYS AFTER                56
    THE DEMAND. IF THE RESPONDENT DEMANDS A JURY TRIAL, THE COURT SHALL                  57

    DEMAND. A DELAY ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE RESPONDENT IS EXCLUDED FROM THE                  59

             (10) (16) "In-state host track" means a track, located within the state of                 4
    Colorado, at which a race meet of horses is conducted.                                              5
             (11) (17) (a) "In-state simulcast facility" means:                                         6
             (I) A class A or class B horse track at which a licensee has held within                   7
    the preceding twelve months or is licensed and scheduled to hold within the                         8
    following twelve months a race meet of at least the duration required of a class                    9
    A or class B track for the purpose of handling pari-mutuel wagers as authorized                    10
    by this article 32; or                                                                             11
             (II) An additional facility that is operated by and is the responsibility of              12
    the licensee of a class B horse track, located in Colorado, and used for the                       13
    handling of wagers placed on simulcast races received by the track or facility.                    14
    The number of additional facilities cannot exceed the total number of facilities                   15
    licensed to hold a race meet in 2003 plus one additional facility per licensee as                  16
    authorized under this article 32.                                                                  17
             (b) If an additional facility is jointly owned or operated as a simulcast                 18
    facility by two or more licensees, the additional facility shall be IS deemed to                   19
    be one of the additional simulcast facilities of only one of the licensees, as                     20
    designated in writing to the commission.                                                           21
             (c) The commission, for good cause, may grant a licensed class A horse                    22
    track permission to receive simulcast races at an alternate location within five                   23
    miles of its track during the times when the track is not in operation.                            24
             (12) (18) "Interstate common pool" means a pari-mutuel pool                               25
    established at one location, usually but not necessarily at a host track, within                   26
    which pool are combined comparable pari-mutuel pools of one or more                                27
    simulcast facilities upon a race run at the host track for purposes of establishing                28
    payoff prices in the various states. There may be simulcast facilities in more                     29
    than one state simultaneously combining pari-mutuel pools into the common                          30
    pool of the host track. Where permitted by the laws and rules of the states in                     31
    which the host track and the simulcast facilities are located and with the                         32
    concurrence of the host track, the combined pari-mutuel pool may be                                33
    established on a regional or other basis between two or more simulcast facilities                  34
    and need not involve a merger into the host track's pari-mutuel pool. In such                      35
    instances, one of the simulcast facilities shall serve as if it were the host track                36
    for the purposes of holding the common pool and calculating payoffs. The                           37
    interstate common pool shall be as specified in the written simulcast racing                       38
    agreement between the host track and the person operating the simulcast facility                   39
    receiving the simulcast races.                                                                     40
             (13) (19) "Intrastate common pool" means a pari-mutuel pool,                              41
    established for an in-state host track, that includes wagers made at the in-state                  42
    host track as well as wagers made at in-state simulcast facilities on simulcast                    43
    races of live races run at the in-state host track.                                                44
